hypotheses.mechanism: Swaps are NOT physical linking errors. On the ef graph (all 199 videos, tail npz + GT geff), in only 6.2% of the 1528 swaps are both matched nodes within 2.5 um of their GT points. 88.5% have one side >3 um (median GT-to-node 4.35 um, second-nearest node 6.4 um, GT step only 2.47 um, while the 'true' link p_u->p_v is 9.3 um long). So the GT point sits between two of our tracks and the 7 um per-frame optimal matcher attaches it to track A at t and track B at t+1: 1 FN + 2 FP per flip. u_diverted and v_taken are the one-sided version (the far side has a median of 3.9 and 4.4 um). Across all 128,883 GT edges the FN rate is a steep function of dmax (the larger of the two GT-to-nearest-node distances): 0.9% at 2-2.5 um, 1.8% at 2.5-3, 4.5% at 3.5-4, 10.6% at 4-5 and 28% at 5-7 um. 93% of all FN have dmax >2.5 um and only 447 FN have dmax <=2.5. The GT-minus-node offsets persist along tracks (frame-to-frame correlation z 0.70, y 0.67, x 0.64) and carry a constant bias. Per video, in voxels: 6bba z +0.44 / y +0.72 / x +0.48 (z>0 in 98% of videos); 44b6 z +0.09 / y +0.49 / x -0.09 (y>0 in 92%). GT coordinates are integer voxels, and our writer does z=max(0,int(round(z))), which discards linefit's sub-voxel precision and ignores the bias. Removing the bias shrinks exactly the distances that make matches flip. Naive intensity centroiding makes things worse (median 1.72->1.90 um), and a GBM on patch features gets R2~0 per axis, so only the constant part is robustly predictable without the learned head.
hypotheses.change: In write_test_submission (after linefit, after all linking), write float coordinates plus a constant per-axis offset in voxels: dz=+0.25..0.3, dy=+0.5, dx=+0.2..0.3 (i.e. +0.4-0.5 um z, +0.2 um y, +0.1 um x), clipped to the volume. Topology, node count and edges stay unchanged, so only the scorer's matching changes. After the coordhead port lands: dump head-refined coordinates for ~20 train videos, measure the residual mean GT-node offset per axis, and set the offset to about half of the residual (shrinkage 0.5 was best in CV: alpha 0.5 cut the >3 um tail from 15.8% to 10.4% on 44b6 and from 15.4% to 12.1% on 6bba; alpha 1.0 was worse).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Distance model on all 199 videos (FN(dmax) curve applied to the shifted coordinates; current rounded output = 739+5440 modelled FN): float only gives 718+5285 (-176 FN, part of the port). Float+0.3 vox all axes gives 725+4914 (-364 vs float, -540 vs rounded). Float+0.5 vox gives 757+4837 (-448 on 6bba). Each FN recovered also removes about 0.93 FP units (swap/u_div competitor edges). 1 unit = 7.4e-6 score (calibrated: swap oracle 1528+0.93*3003 = 4321 units = 0.032; the check on u_div predicts 0.0083 against 0.0080 measured). Ceiling for the constant part: (364..448)*1.93*7.4e-6 = +0.0052..+0.0064 locally, almost all on 6bba; 44b6 moves -0.0001..-0.0005.
hypotheses.lab_test: No re-linking is needed. Take the lab's final graphs (exp39 + ef_a3_rl_pr), rewrite only the node coordinates (float, plus the offset grid dz in {0,0.25,0.5}, dy in {0,0.5}, dx in {0,0.25} voxels), and rescore with tools/score_geffs.py (official). Grid on SELECTION (64 6bba), then one CONFIRMATION run. Always report float-with-no-shift as its own control, because float alone belongs to the port. Success: confirmation >= +0.002 over float, 6bba >= +0.002, 44b6 >= -0.0005 (44b6 z bias is only +0.09 vox, so no gain is expected there), node count identical. Minutes on a Kaggle CPU kernel.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.002..+0.005 over float coordinates (model: 364 FN * 1.93 units * 7.4e-6 = 0.0052, discounted 30-60% because the dmax->FN curve is partly confounded with density). Public LB +0.000..+0.004, depending on whether the test embryos carry 6bba-like (+0.44 vox z) or 44b6-like (+0.09 vox) bias. The y component (+0.5 vox in both embryos) is the robust part but small in um (0.2 um).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. The bias is embryo-dependent (z +0.44 vs +0.09 vox), and the test embryos are unseen. A forum user (Le Quang Canh) reported that a constant dz correction lost 0.003 on HIS pipeline, which may differ in its rounding/linefit. The ported head was trained on GT, so it may already absorb the bias. Measure the residual before shipping, and ship the half-shift (shrinkage) version as a hedge.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Closed lines are 'global-shift relink' (a shift used inside the RELINK cost, which cannot matter because relink is translation-invariant) and detector/TTA changes. This one changes only the written coordinates after linking. It exploits a measured +0.5-voxel GT convention bias and the int(round()) in our writer, and no probe has tested it. It builds on sub-voxel (float) output rather than re-proposing the head port.

hypotheses.mechanism: The motion relink REPLACES the ILP edge set, and its relaxed gate is 10 um, so any ILP edge longer than 10 um (or one that loses both Hungarian passes) cannot be reproduced. The ILP's own decision is thrown away, and both nodes end up as a free end and a free start. FN anatomy: b_break = 399 FN, of which 281 have ILP provenance (dist median 9.9 um, 75th percentile 11.8 um, i.e. at or beyond the gate). These nodes are WELL localised (median GT-node distance 1.87 um vs 4.35 for swaps), so here the linking decision really is wrong, unlike swaps. End->start pairs that the ILP linked are 271 TP / 19 FP (93.4% precision), and 231 TP / 8 FP at p>=0.7. The measured stitch gives +0.0021 on confirmation (44b6 +0.00117, 6bba +0.00247). It 'failed' only the >=55%-of-videos-gaining criterion, because 44b6 has so few events that 85% of its videos are untouched (a gain can only occur on videos with an event).
hypotheses.change: After the edge filter (before linefit), for every free end u at t and free start v at t+1 where (u,v) is an edge of the raw ILP solution with p>=0.7, add u->v. Never create forks or merges. Apply in deterministic (t, u) order, and each endpoint can be claimed once. Implementation: tools/build_probe_kernel.py stitch_final_graph rule st_p07. Also re-test a variant that additionally restores the ILP edge when the edge filter dropped the relink replacement of an ILP-linked node, which catches the 27+23 u_div/v_taken FN with ILP provenance.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Oracle for breaks = +0.00298 (399 FN units; the 7.4e-6/unit calibration gives 0.0030). The ILP-provenance subset is 281 FN, so ceiling ~ 281*7.4e-6 = +0.0021, which matches the measured st_all. Plus <=50 u_div/v_taken ILP-provenance FN = +0.0004. Total ceiling ~ +0.0025.
hypotheses.lab_test: Already implemented. Re-run st_p07 and st_all on CONFIRMATION on top of exp39+ef (and on the 5.5-um rebuilt cache when it is ready). Replace the '>=55% of videos gaining' criterion, for sparse-event rules, with: (a) a sign test over AFFECTED videos only (videos with >=1 added edge), (b) no video loses more than 0.0005, and (c) each embryo delta >= +0.0005. Success: confirmation >= +0.0015 overall and 44b6 >= +0.0008.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0017..+0.0021 (measured). LB +0.0005..+0.0015, discounted for the in-sample ILP/edge network. At 93-97% precision, even a 2x drop in precision on unseen embryos stays positive (the break-even precision is 48%).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low. The rule is additive only (no node changes, no forks) and very precise. The main risk is the small absolute size, which falls inside LB noise, so bundle it with another change rather than spending a lone probe on it.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: It is not a relink knob (gate/bonus) and not the closed readmit/gap-filler family (those create nodes or bridge gaps from geometry). It restores the ILP's own scored decisions that the relink structurally cannot reproduce. The brief lists it as 'fails the per-embryo gate', not as closed, and the failure is a property of the gate on sparse events, not a negative delta (44b6 +0.00117 >= +0.001).

hypotheses.mechanism: The swap oracle (+0.032) and the u_div/v_taken oracle (+0.016) are mostly unreachable by re-assignment. Linking p_u->p_v would connect two DIFFERENT physical cells 9.3 um apart when the GT cell moved only 2.5 um. The 2x2/2-opt acceleration-based moves in swap_anatomy.py favour physically smooth tracks, and those tracks are already the smooth ones. The earlier finding 'velocity picks the truth 0/381 on contested links' says the same. The only genuinely fixable cases are the ones where both nodes are well localised: 6.2% of swaps (~95 FN), 16.4% of u_div (~97) and 10.8% of v_taken (~60). In these the network barely scored the true pair (ckpt_prob present for 0.8% of swaps, 19.6% of u_div, 8.3% of v_taken), because the kNN candidate graph omits it and the notebook discards all non-ILP candidate scores before post-processing.
hypotheses.change: Run the existing swap_anatomy.py --eval on SELECTION with rules that accept a 2x2 swap (a->b,c->d => a->d,c->b) or a repoint (a->b => a->d with d a free start; plus the not-yet-implemented backward repoint c->d => a->d with a a free end) ONLY when all of these hold: all four nodes lie on tracks of length >= 5; the new edges are no longer than 1.5x the local median step; the multi-frame acceleration (t-1..t+2) improves by >= 1.0 um; and, if the kernel is extended to dump the edge transformer's kNN candidate scores, the new pair's network probability is >= 0.5. Close the line if selection is below +0.001.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Only the well-localised fraction counts. Swaps: 95 FN + 190 competitor FP = 95+177 = 272 units * 7.4e-6 = +0.0020. u_div: 97 FN + 92 FP = 183 units = +0.0014. v_taken: 60+56 = 116 units = +0.0009. Total ceiling about +0.0043, versus the headline +0.048 oracle.
hypotheses.lab_test: swap_anatomy.py --eval --split selection --ef alt=3,relink=1,prune=1 with a rules JSON (3-6 rules). This needs a Kaggle CPU run of about 20-40 min. Success: selection >= +0.001 with net FP not increasing. Otherwise record the line as closed with this ceiling.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.0003..+0.001 locally (20-30% of the +0.0043 ceiling), about 0 to +0.0005 on LB. Its main value is stopping further work on a +0.032 'oracle' that is a matching artefact.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low risk, low reward. It uses in-sample network scores if extended, and on unseen embryos the acceleration criterion may flip more correct links than wrong ones.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed list covers relink knobs and alternative association methods (mutual-best, flow-prior, HOCT, Trackastra). A targeted local 2x2/repoint repair on the FINAL graph restricted to well-localised, multi-frame-inconsistent pairs has not been evaluated, and the tool already exists (swap_anatomy.py). This entry supplies the realistic ceiling so that it gets one run, not a campaign.

hypotheses.mechanism: The residual FN mass sits in the 4-7 um dmax band: 11,125 GT edges holding ~2,064 FN (34% of all FN) and 69% of swaps (1,049/1,528). There each 0.5 um of distance changes the FN rate by several points (4.5% at 3.5-4 um vs 10.6% at 4-5 um vs 28% at 5-7 um). The ported x138 head applies a scaled (the 's075' weights imply scale 0.75) and clipped (<=2 um) shift that was tuned on x138's pipeline, not ours. Our pipeline additionally applies linefit (w0.8, win2), whose 5-frame averaging interacts with per-frame head noise. GT-node offsets are persistent (frame-to-frame correlation 0.64-0.75), so a stronger scale is plausible after linefit averaging. In our crude-feature CV, however, alpha 0.5-0.75 beat alpha 1.0, so the optimum must be measured, not assumed. Linefit window/weight itself is NOT the lever: (2, 0.8) stays best under float output on the one video tested, and B28 already closed it.
hypotheses.change: After the coordhead port: make head scale s in {0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25} and clip c in {2.0, 3.0} um env-configurable (the default stays 0.75/2.0). Choose them by minimising official-scorer loss on final-coordinate-only rescoring (topology fixed at the port's graph), then probe the best setting once. Optional (only if s=1.25 or c=3 wins): retrain the 224->32->3 MLP on frozen UNet features at GT-matched peaks with a Huber loss on (GT - peak), without clip, on 6bba selection videos.
hypotheses.upper_bound: The 4-7 um band holds ~2,064 FN. The distance model gives -1,058 FN (all distances shrunk 10%) or -1,797 (shrunk 20%) over the whole population. Halving that for confounding, the full head accounts for ~500-900 FN = +0.007..+0.013 (x 1.93 units x 7.4e-6), consistent with x138's +0.007 LB. The incremental share from re-tuning scale/clip is at most ~25% of that: +0.002..+0.003.
hypotheses.lab_test: Needs head outputs on train. In the port's Kaggle GPU kernel, add a dump mode that writes raw peaks + raw head shift vectors for ~30 selection videos (1 seed, no TTA, ~20-30 GPU-min). Offline (Kaggle CPU): map those shifts onto the lab's final graph nodes by id/position, apply scale/clip, run linefit, rescore (official). Success: best (s,c) beats (0.75, 2.0) by >= +0.0015 on selection AND on a 44b6 hold-out slice, then one LB probe against exp51.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.000..+0.003 on LB over the plain port. A zero result is informative too: it means the port already captures the positional lever, and the remaining gap lies in the 46% of FN with dmax >7 um (detection misses), not in linking.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium to high. The head and the UNet features are in-sample on train (the public weights were trained on these videos), so the local optimum of s may be too aggressive. Favour the more conservative setting when two settings are within 0.001, and use the single probe as the arbiter.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: It is not the port itself (which ships x138's defaults) and not a detector fine-tune or a TTA variant. It calibrates the sub-voxel refinement to our pipeline's linefit and to the metric's matching-flip curve, which is new evidence from the swap anatomy (swaps are localisation-driven). Linefit re-tuning alone was closed (B28), and I do not re-propose it.
